about: Building codes, one entry each, read by `building_code` and `stair_check` (codes.rs). A project names one and starts with its rules, which it may change (a state's or a city's own rules); nothing built is ever refused for breaking one, only reported. A country's code is added as a new entry, never as code. UNCHECKED: the numbers were typed from memory of the documents named, not from their text, and each code tells occupancies apart where an entry holds one row (the general one); check a number against a copy before relying on it. Where a code gives no number, the entry holds a forgiving one that asks nothing in practice, and `note` says which. Millimetres. `stairs`: `riser` and `going` are what a new stair starts with; `riser_min`..`riser_max` and `going_min`..`going_max` their ranges; `step_min`..`step_max` the range of 2 risers + 1 going; `width_min` the least clear width; `headroom` the least height over the walk line; a landing is due when a flight would rise more than `flight_rise_max` or hold more than `flight_risers_max` risers, whichever comes first; `landing_rule` says how long a landing must be: `width` the stair's width, `landing_length` being enough; `fixed` `landing_length`; `step` a going and one step (2 risers + 1 going), and `landing_length` at least. `winders` whether winding treads are allowed; `walk_line` where their going is measured: `centre` along the middle, `narrow_side` at `walk_line_offset` from the narrow side; `winder_going_min` the least going there and `winder_narrow_min` the least at the narrow end. `nosing_max` the most a tread overhangs; `open_risers` whether risers may be open; `uniformity` the most two risers or goings of a flight may differ; `handrail_min`..`handrail_max` a handrail's height over the nosings; `guard_min` a guard's least height.

codes.name: No building code
codes.note: No code's numbers: wide ranges round common practice, so a stair is reported only when it is far from any stair one would build.

codes.name: ABNT NBR 9050 and NBR 9077
codes.note: A state's fire brigade often rules instead of NBR 9077 (São Paulo's IT 11, for one): change the rules to its numbers. Winders are not allowed on an accessible route or an emergency stair, so they are reported; the walk line and its goings are forgiving numbers, and so are the most risers in a flight and the uniformity. The handrail range holds NBR 9050's two rails, at 700 and 920.

codes.name: International Building Code
codes.note: The general row; inside a dwelling the IBC and the IRC allow a riser of 7 3/4 in and a going of 10 in. The IBC has no step rule and counts no risers in a flight: `step_min`, `step_max`, `going_max` and `flight_risers_max` are forgiving numbers. Winders are allowed inside dwellings only. Inches, written in millimetres.

codes.name: DIN 18065
codes.note: The row for buildings in general; a house of up to two dwellings may have a width of 800, a riser of 200 and a going from 230. The European Union has no stair code of its own: each country has one, and this is Germany's. DIN counts risers, 18 in a flight at most, so `flight_rise_max` is a forgiving number, and so is `nosing_max`.

codes.name: Building Standards Law of Japan
references: Building Standards Law Enforcement Order, articles 23 to 25 (stairs, landings, handrails)
codes.note: The row for buildings not otherwise listed; schools, theatres and large shops have stricter rows, a dwelling a looser one. A winder's going is measured 300 from its narrow end. The order gives no riser minimum, going maximum, step rule, headroom, riser count or uniformity: those are forgiving numbers.
